text:
**Refined prompt:** Enumerate every RealWorld API route reachable without a token, answering as a security reviewer, with each claim cited to file:line from the actual `configure()` blocks and controllers — answer first, evidence after. · Assumptions: "without logging in" = no `Authorization` header at all; I'm listing all HTTP routes, not just the spec'd ones.

**Nine endpoints are public, and one of them is `DELETE /api/users/:slug` — an unauthenticated account deletion.** Auth is enforced only by `AuthMiddleware` registered per route in three `configure()` blocks; there are no guards anywhere else, so every route not in those lists is open.

## Public (no token needed)

| Endpoint | Handler |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/` | `src/app.controller.ts:5` |
| `POST /api/users` (register) | `src/user/user.controller.ts:32` |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:43` |
| **`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** | `src/user/user.controller.ts:37` |
| `GET /api/articles` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:24` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:38` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:43` |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18` |
| `GET /api/tags` | `src/tag/tag.controller.ts:17` |

Global prefix `api` is set at `src/main.ts:8`.

## The one that matters

```ts
// src/user/user.controller.ts:37-40
@Delete('users/:slug')
async delete(@Param() params) {
  return await this.userService.delete(params.slug);
}
```
```ts
// src/user/user.service.ts:83-85
async delete(email: string): Promise<DeleteResult> {
  return await this.userRepository.delete({ email: email});
}
```

`:slug` is passed straight through as an **email**. `UserModule.configure()` applies `AuthMiddleware` to `user` GET and PUT only (`src/user/user.module.ts:20`) — nothing covers `users/:slug`. So `DELETE /api/users/someone@example.com` from an anonymous client deletes that account. No token, no ownership comparison. `TagModule.configure()` is empty (`src/tag/tag.module.ts:17-18`), which is fine for `GET /tags` but confirms the pattern: absent from a `forRoutes` list = public.

## Guarded, for contrast

- `GET /user`, `PUT /user` — `src/user/user.module.ts:20`
- `GET /articles/feed`, `POST /articles`, `PUT|DELETE /articles/:slug`, `POST /articles/:slug/comments`, `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`, `POST|DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` — `src/article/article.module.ts:24-31`
- `profiles/:username/follow`, all methods — `src/profile/profile.module.ts:22`

Two caveats on "guarded": it means *authenticated*, not *authorized*. `PUT /articles/:slug` (`src/article/article.controller.ts:59-63`) and `DELETE /articles/:slug` (`:68-71`) never receive the caller's id at all — any logged-in user can edit or delete any article. The `@ApiResponse({status: 403})` decorators on those handlers document behaviour that isn't implemented. That's already on the board in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`; the unguarded `DELETE /users/:slug` is not.

**What I did not read:** `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` and `src/user/user.decorator.ts` this turn — I verified route *registration* directly, but my description of what the middleware does on a bad token is from `.claude/knowledge/auth.md`, not re-read source. I did grep the whole of `src/` for `UseGuards|APP_GUARD|CanActivate|forRoutes` and found only the three `forRoutes` calls above, so I'm confident nothing else enforces auth.
